  \else\usebox{\pandoc@box}%
  \fi%
}

\DocumentationTok{\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\# Project 1 \#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#}
\CommentTok{\# Digital Strategies for the Social Sciences}
\CommentTok{\# Project 1: Scraping event information from Visit Stockholm}
\CommentTok{\#}
\CommentTok{\# Website: https://www.visitstockholm.com/events/}
\CommentTok{\#}
\CommentTok{\# The idea here is to build a small dataset about events happening in Stockholm}
\CommentTok{\# by scraping the Visit Stockholm events page. I download the HTML, figure out}
\CommentTok{\# where the data actually lives in the page structure, extract it, and then}
\CommentTok{\# enrich it with geolocation data from an API.}
\DocumentationTok{\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#}


\CommentTok{\# 1. PACKAGES}
\CommentTok{\# I need httr to send HTTP requests, XML to parse the HTML, stringi to deal}
\CommentTok{\# with encoding (Stockholm has a lot of Swedish characters that can go wrong),}
\CommentTok{\# jsonlite to work with the API response, and readr to save the final CSV.}

\CommentTok{\#install.packages(c("httr", "XML", "stringi", "jsonlite", "readr"))}

\FunctionTok{library}\NormalTok{(httr)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Confirming the class is indeed raw.}

\FunctionTok{class}\NormalTok{(response}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{content)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
## [1] "raw"
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Converting the raw response into a readable HTML string using UTF{-}8 encoding.}

\NormalTok{html }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{content}\NormalTok{(response, }\AttributeTok{as =} \StringTok{"text"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{encoding =} \StringTok{"UTF{-}8"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Checking the encoding of the result.}

\FunctionTok{Encoding}\NormalTok{(html)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
## [1] "UTF-8"
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Using stringi to double{-}check the encoding detection.}
\CommentTok{\# This helped me confirm that UTF{-}8 was the right choice for this page.}

\FunctionTok{stri\_enc\_detect}\NormalTok{(response}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{content)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
## [[1]]
##       Encoding Language Confidence
## 1        UTF-8                1.00
## 2 windows-1252       en       0.43
## 3 windows-1250       ro       0.24
## 4     UTF-16BE                0.10
## 5     UTF-16LE                0.10
## 6 windows-1254       tr       0.07
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 5. SAVE AND RELOAD THE HTML}

\CommentTok{\# Saving the HTML locally so I don\textquotesingle{}t have to re{-}request the page every time}
\CommentTok{\# I run the script while testing. This was very useful during development}
\CommentTok{\# because I could just reload the saved file instead of hitting the server}
\CommentTok{\# over and over.}

\FunctionTok{writeLines}\NormalTok{(html, }\StringTok{"visitstockholm.html"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Reading the saved file back in.}

\NormalTok{lines }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{readLines}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"visitstockholm.html"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{encoding =} \StringTok{"UTF{-}8"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Joining the lines back into one HTML string.}

\NormalTok{html }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{paste0}\NormalTok{(lines, }\AttributeTok{collapse =} \StringTok{"}\SpecialCharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}



\CommentTok{\# 6. PARSE THE HTML AND CHECK IF THE DATA IS THERE}

\CommentTok{\# Parsing the HTML into a DOM tree so I can use XPath to navigate the structure.}
\CommentTok{\# XPath doesn\textquotesingle{}t work on raw text strings, it needs the parsed tree.}

\NormalTok{dom }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{htmlParse}\NormalTok{(html)}

\CommentTok{\# Before doing anything else, I wanted to check if the event data is actually}
\CommentTok{\# embedded in the HTML, or if it loads dynamically with JavaScript.}
\CommentTok{\# If this returns TRUE, I don\textquotesingle{}t need Selenium — the data is already there.}

\FunctionTok{grepl}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"The Hornstull Market"}\NormalTok{, html)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
## [1] TRUE
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 7. EXPLORE THE PAGE STRUCTURE AND EXTRACT NAMES + LINKS}

\CommentTok{\# I tested different tags to figure out where the useful information was stored.}
\CommentTok{\# This exploration step was important because the page doesn\textquotesingle{}t use obvious}
\CommentTok{\# semantic tags for its event data.}

\FunctionTok{xpathSApply}\NormalTok{(dom, }\StringTok{"//h1"}\NormalTok{, xmlValue)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}

\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\FunctionTok{xpathSApply}\NormalTok{(dom, }\StringTok{"//h2"}\NormalTok{, xmlValue)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# From testing, h3 tags contain the event names and a tags contain the links.}



\CommentTok{\# Extracting event names from h3 elements.}

\NormalTok{event\_names }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{xpathSApply}\NormalTok{(dom, }\StringTok{"//h3"}\NormalTok{, xmlValue)}

\CommentTok{\# Removing extra whitespace.}

\NormalTok{event\_names }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{trimws}\NormalTok{(event\_names)}

\CommentTok{\# Extracting all links from the page.}

\NormalTok{all\_links }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{xpathSApply}\NormalTok{(dom, }\StringTok{"//a"}\NormalTok{, xmlGetAttr, }\StringTok{"href"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Keeping only links that match the Visit Stockholm event URL pattern.}
\CommentTok{\# I used a regular expression here to filter out navigation links,}
\CommentTok{\# footer links, and other things that are not event pages.}

\NormalTok{event\_links }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ all\_links[}
  \FunctionTok{grepl}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"https://www.visitstockholm.com/events/.*/next/"}\NormalTok{, all\_links)}
\NormalTok{]}

\CommentTok{\# Checking that names and links have the same length before combining them.}

\FunctionTok{length}\NormalTok{(event\_names)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# The pattern I found: event name, category, event name again,}
\CommentTok{\# "Calendar icon", date, "Location icon", location.}
\CommentTok{\# Once I saw this, I could use "Calendar icon" as an anchor to extract}
\CommentTok{\# everything around it.}



\CommentTok{\# 9. EXTRACT CATEGORIES, DATES, AND LOCATIONS}

\CommentTok{\# Cleaning up whitespace and removing empty text nodes.}

\NormalTok{all\_text }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{trimws}\NormalTok{(all\_text)}

\NormalTok{all\_text }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ all\_text[all\_text }\SpecialCharTok{!=} \StringTok{""}\NormalTok{]}

\CommentTok{\# Finding all positions where "Calendar icon" appears in the text vector.}
\CommentTok{\# The date is always one position after this.}

\NormalTok{calendar\_positions }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{which}\NormalTok{(all\_text }\SpecialCharTok{==} \StringTok{"Calendar icon"}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{calendar\_positions}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
##  [1]  60  87  94 101 108 116 123 130 137 145 152 159 166 174 181 188 195 203 210
## [20] 217 224 232 239 246 253 261 268 275 282
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# The first "Calendar icon" is in the filter section at the top of the page,}
\CommentTok{\# not from an actual event. I filter those out by checking whether the next}
\CommentTok{\# element is actually a month name. If it\textquotesingle{}s not, it\textquotesingle{}s not a real event date.}

\NormalTok{month\_pattern }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \StringTok{"Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec"}

\NormalTok{calendar\_positions }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ calendar\_positions[}
  \FunctionTok{grepl}\NormalTok{(month\_pattern, all\_text[calendar\_positions }\SpecialCharTok{+} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{])}
\NormalTok{]}

\NormalTok{calendar\_positions}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
##  [1]  87  94 101 108 116 123 130 137 145 152 159 166 174 181 188 195 203 210 217
## [20] 224 232 239 246 253 261 268 275 282
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Extracting information based on the fixed pattern around "Calendar icon":}
\CommentTok{\# category  = 2 positions before Calendar icon}
\CommentTok{\# event name = 1 position before Calendar icon}
\CommentTok{\# date       = 1 position after Calendar icon}
\CommentTok{\# location   = 3 positions after Calendar icon}

\NormalTok{event\_categories }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ all\_text[calendar\_positions }\SpecialCharTok{{-}} \DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{]}

\NormalTok{event\_names }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ all\_text[calendar\_positions }\SpecialCharTok{{-}} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}

\NormalTok{event\_dates }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ all\_text[calendar\_positions }\SpecialCharTok{+} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}

\NormalTok{event\_locations }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ all\_text[calendar\_positions }\SpecialCharTok{+} \DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{]}

\CommentTok{\# Checking lengths before creating the dataset.}

\FunctionTok{length}\NormalTok{(event\_names)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 11. VISIT INDIVIDUAL EVENT PAGES}

\CommentTok{\# The project requires the crawler to visit at least two pages automatically.}
\CommentTok{\# Here I loop through the event links and visit each individual event page}
\CommentTok{\# to extract more detailed information: description, venue, street address, and city.}
\CommentTok{\#}
\CommentTok{\# This is where the scraper moves beyond just the listing page and actually}
\CommentTok{\# follows each event to its own subpage.}

\NormalTok{subpage\_title }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{()}
\NormalTok{subpage\_status }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{()}
\NormalTok{event\_description }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{()}
\NormalTok{subpage\_venue }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{()}
\NormalTok{subpage\_street\_address }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{()}
\NormalTok{subpage\_postal\_code }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{()}
\NormalTok{subpage\_city }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{()}

\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ (i }\ControlFlowTok{in} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{:}\FunctionTok{nrow}\NormalTok{(events\_df\_clean)) \{}
  
\NormalTok{  event\_url }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ events\_df\_clean}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{link[i]}
  
  \CommentTok{\# Printing progress so I can see what is happening while it runs.}
  
  \FunctionTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{paste}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Downloading subpage"}\NormalTok{, i, }\StringTok{"of"}\NormalTok{, }\FunctionTok{nrow}\NormalTok{(events\_df\_clean)))}
  
  \CommentTok{\# Downloading the individual event page.}
  
\NormalTok{  event\_response }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{GET}\NormalTok{(event\_url)}
  
  \CommentTok{\# Saving the status code for each subpage.}
  
\NormalTok{  subpage\_status[i] }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ event\_response}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{status\_code}
  
  \CommentTok{\# Converting to readable HTML text.}
  
\NormalTok{  event\_html }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{content}\NormalTok{(event\_response, }\AttributeTok{as =} \StringTok{"text"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{encoding =} \StringTok{"UTF{-}8"}\NormalTok{)}
  
  \CommentTok{\# Parsing the subpage HTML into a DOM tree.}
  
\NormalTok{  event\_dom }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{htmlParse}\NormalTok{(event\_html)}
  
  \CommentTok{\# Extracting the h1 title from the subpage.}
  
\NormalTok{  title }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{xpathSApply}\NormalTok{(event\_dom, }\StringTok{"//h1"}\NormalTok{, xmlValue)}
\NormalTok{  title }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{trimws}\NormalTok{(title)}
  
  \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ (}\FunctionTok{length}\NormalTok{(title) }\SpecialCharTok{==} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{) \{}
\NormalTok{    title }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \ConstantTok{NA}
\NormalTok{  \}}
  
\NormalTok{  subpage\_title[i] }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ title[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}
  
  
  \CommentTok{\# Collecting all text elements from the subpage.}
  
\NormalTok{  page\_text }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{xpathSApply}\NormalTok{(event\_dom, }\StringTok{"//*[text()]"}\NormalTok{, xmlValue)}
  
\NormalTok{  page\_text }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{trimws}\NormalTok{(page\_text)}
  
\NormalTok{  page\_text }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ page\_text[page\_text }\SpecialCharTok{!=} \StringTok{""}\NormalTok{]}
  
  
  \CommentTok{\# The event description usually appears right before "All dates" in the}
  \CommentTok{\# text order. I use that as an anchor — same idea as on the main page.}
  
\NormalTok{  all\_dates\_position }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{which}\NormalTok{(page\_text }\SpecialCharTok{==} \StringTok{"All dates"}\NormalTok{)}
  
  \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ (}\FunctionTok{length}\NormalTok{(all\_dates\_position) }\SpecialCharTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{) \{}
\NormalTok{    event\_description[i] }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ page\_text[all\_dates\_position[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{] }\SpecialCharTok{{-}} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{  \} }\ControlFlowTok{else}\NormalTok{ \{}
\NormalTok{    event\_description[i] }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \ConstantTok{NA}
\NormalTok{  \}}
  
  
  \CommentTok{\# The address section follows a "Getting there" heading on each subpage.}
  \CommentTok{\# After "Getting there" comes: Location icon, venue name, street address, city.}
  \CommentTok{\# But some pages also include a postal code between the street address and city,}
  \CommentTok{\# so I handle both cases with a regex check.}
  
\NormalTok{  getting\_there\_position }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{which}\NormalTok{(page\_text }\SpecialCharTok{==} \StringTok{"Getting there"}\NormalTok{)}
  
  \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ (}\FunctionTok{length}\NormalTok{(getting\_there\_position) }\SpecialCharTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{) \{}
    
\NormalTok{    pos }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ getting\_there\_position[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}
    
\NormalTok{    subpage\_venue[i] }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ page\_text[pos }\SpecialCharTok{+} \DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{    subpage\_street\_address[i] }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ page\_text[pos }\SpecialCharTok{+} \DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{]}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Swedish postal codes look like "121 77" or "11138".}
    \CommentTok{\# This regex checks if the next value matches that pattern.}
    \CommentTok{\# If it does, I extract it separately; if not, I skip it and go straight to the city.}
    
\NormalTok{    possible\_postal\_code }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ page\_text[pos }\SpecialCharTok{+} \DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{    possible\_city }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ page\_text[pos }\SpecialCharTok{+} \DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{]}
    
\NormalTok{    postal\_code\_pattern }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \StringTok{"\^{}}\SpecialCharTok{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}}\StringTok{d\{3\}}\SpecialCharTok{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}}\StringTok{s?}\SpecialCharTok{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}}\StringTok{d\{2\}$"}
    
    \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ (}\FunctionTok{grepl}\NormalTok{(postal\_code\_pattern, possible\_postal\_code)) \{}
      
\NormalTok{      subpage\_postal\_code[i] }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ possible\_postal\_code}
\NormalTok{      subpage\_city[i] }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ possible\_city}
      
\NormalTok{    \} }\ControlFlowTok{else}\NormalTok{ \{}
      
\NormalTok{      subpage\_postal\_code[i] }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \ConstantTok{NA}
\NormalTok{      subpage\_city[i] }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ possible\_postal\_code}
\NormalTok{    \}}
    
\NormalTok{  \} }\ControlFlowTok{else}\NormalTok{ \{}
    
    \CommentTok{\# If the page doesn\textquotesingle{}t have a "Getting there" section, storing NA.}
    
\NormalTok{    subpage\_venue[i] }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \ConstantTok{NA}
\NormalTok{    subpage\_street\_address[i] }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \ConstantTok{NA}
\NormalTok{    subpage\_postal\_code[i] }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \ConstantTok{NA}
\NormalTok{    subpage\_city[i] }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \ConstantTok{NA}
\NormalTok{  \}}
  
  
  \CommentTok{\# Pausing between requests to be polite to the server and avoid getting blocked.}
  
  \FunctionTok{Sys.sleep}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\NormalTok{events\_df\_clean}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{subpage\_title }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ subpage\_title}

##                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      event_description
## 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Hornstulls Marknad is a public market taking place every Saturday and Sunday, from the first weekend of April to the last weekend in September (except for the midsummer weekend in June). Flea, vintage, design, art, crafts, antiques, literature, delicatessen, foodstuffs and much more.
## 2                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Welcome to Stockholm’s folkmusic oasis: Skeppis – the house of folk music! The unique cultural space hosts jam sessions, concerts, workshops, social dancing to live acoustic music, food, and drinks (non-alcoholic). Open to all newcomers, beginners and experienced visitors. The venue offers a variety of activities, and everything is run non-profit in the spirit of folkmusic!
## 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The myth of the violent, plundering Vikings (with horned helmets) has been circulating for a long time. But what do we really know about life in Nordic countries one thousand years ago?
## 4                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Springbeast Festival is a street art and music festival in Snösätra, Stockholm, May 14–17, 2026. Over 90 artists from 20+ countries create live graffiti and murals, alongside 30+ hours of music with artists like Loop Troop Rockers and Linda Pira. Expect street food, workshops, talks, and activities for all ages.
## 5                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The artist Kim Andreas Roland Berger has been awarded the Fredrik Roos Art Grant for 2026. In connection with the award, Artipelag presents Roland Berger’s grant exhibition, Accumulated Stacks. Kim Andreas Roland Berger (b. 1993 in Oslo) uses drawing, painting and sculpture in his material-based and process-oriented practice.
## 6                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     In this all-Italian program with Ensemble BaraBarock, tears, jealousy, desire, and ecstasy resonate. In the Venice of love, there is "the Red Priest" Antonio Vivaldi, one of the most significant composers of the Baroque era.
## 7                                                                                                                                                                               Quarnevalen is one of Sweden’s most spectacular student events, a proud tradition of joy and creativity since 1910. Students from across Stockholm design and build their own creations and parade them before an audience of half a million spectators. It’s the birthplace of innovation and future leaders, even the King once took part as a builder! Quarnevalen is more than a celebration; it’s an essential part of Stockholm’s cultural life.
## 8                                                                                                                              An exhibition by contemporary artist Alia Ali, who works across photography, video, and installation. Known for her visually striking photographic works in which body, textile, and identity intertwine, Ali explores in the exhibition Scapes the boundaries between the individual and the collective, and between visibility and anonymity. Her work has previously been exhibited internationally in the United States, Africa, and the Middle East, an this exhibition marks her debut in Sweden.
## 9                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            In recent years, Dermot Kennedy has gone from being a busker on the street corners of Dublin to becoming one of the most beloved voices in the world. The journey is well-known but still remarkable. When you hear his raspy, almost weathered voice carry melodies filled with both fire and vulnerability, it’s easy to understand how everything happened so quickly.
## 10                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Miami-based artist Earth to Eve creates cinematic alternative pop where personal storytelling meets dark, emotional production. Writing, producing and shaping her entire visual identity herself, she builds a world entirely on her own terms. Now coming to Stockholm for an intimate club show – a chance to discover a rising artist early.
## 11                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                <NA>
## 12                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The restaurant opens at 6 pm, and the concert starts at 8 pm. If you want to have dinner, book a table, otherwise you are welcome to the bar to listen from there. The band plays 3 sets, and you pay 70 SEK per person for the set you listen to.
## 13                                                                                                                                                                                                 Äventyrs is the world's first museum that depicts adventures from all over the world - created to inspire our visitors, awaken dreams and ignite the spark for adventure. In addition to several inspiring exhibitions, there is a large adventure shop and a cafe. Äventyrs also offer an adventure community, education and lectures. The museum is temporary ("pop-up") until midsummer, but hopefully it can remain for longer!
## 14                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Madama Butterfly
## 15                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              12 Points go to… SUS! Forget that worn-out couch at home, we’re taking Eurovision to a whole new level. The grand finale comes to life on the screens.
## 16                                                                                                                                        The hit musical & Julia, which revolves around Max Martin's unique music catalog, is finally being staged at home in Sweden. For several years, the audience- and critically acclaimed musical has filled the halls of the West End and Broadway. & Julia is a modern and humorous reinterpretation of Shakespeare's classic work Romeo & Juliet, but where the story takes completely new turns and everything is turned on its head. Premiere at Cirkus in Stockholm on February 19, 2026.
## 17                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       Kickstart the weekend at Nationalmuseum! On Thursday evenings, the museum is abuzz with people, art and music, with FREE admission for everyone from 5pm to 8pm. Enjoy an ever-changing programme of afterwork drinks, music, workshops and other activities.
## 18                                                                                        At the turn of the 20th century, Alphonse Mucha was one of the most famous artists in Europe. A key figure of Art Nouveau and the inventor of an original style of graphic art, his work combined female beauty and stylised nature with a resolutely innovative composition and typography. The “Mucha style” has been a source of fascination ever since it was created and was applied to a variety of artworks and objects that adorned art lovers’ homes around the world at the time. Welcome to an immersive experience for all ages!
## 19                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   The museum’s largest ever exhibition initiative presents 4,000 artefacts and images in an epic and visual presentation of Nordic cultural history built on the real objects and stories collected by the museum during 150 years.
## 20                                                                                                                                                                                          With our very popular 'Do it Yourself' sessions, you can throw as much (or as little) as you want, create at a speed that works for you, practice specific techniques or just throw for the sake of throwing - All on your own time and under your terms! Instructions are not included. If you would like instructions for how to create ceramics please book a workshop or a course. We do not teach during the Do It yourself sessions.
## 21                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Flatenbastun offers a relaxed lakeside sauna experience by Lake Flaten in southern Stockholm. Here, warmth, nature and refreshing swims come together in a social and welcoming setting for both regulars and first-time guests. Open sauna sessions are available year-round and booked in advance via the website. Bring swimwear and towels for a genuine Swedish sauna experience close to nature.
## 22                                                                                                                                                                                            BAUHAUS-Galan is an annual world-class athletics gala held at Stockholm Olympic Stadium. Many of the competitors consider the Stadium to be the world's most beautiful arena. The world elite is always present, competing against Sweden’s best track and field athletes. The atmosphere at the Stadium is always magical, with its history combined with modern technology and an audience seated just one meter from the competitors.
## 23                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Welcome to the Elitloppet weekend 2026 – one of Sweden's biggest sporting events. Every year, thousands of people visit Solvalla to experience a festive atmosphere with the world's fastest horses and the world's best audience!
## 24                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   The Art of Loving
## 25                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               Photo: Robert Höglund
## 26                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               Linkin Park, who recently received the "Favorite Rock Song" award at the American Music Awards, can now confirm that their acclaimed From Zero World Tour will be extended with new selected European dates in 2026. The tour will kick off on Friday, May 29, with a highly anticipated concert at 3Arena in Stockholm – the band's only performance in the Nordic region next year.
## 27 The adidas Stockholm Marathon takes you through the streets of a beautiful European capital built on 14 islands. The course of this race offers spectacular views of a unique city with varied scenery, including nature and an impeccably preserved medieval city center. The enthusiastic crowds will cheer you along the route and lead you to an unforgettable finish at the 1912 Olympic Stadium, the home of 83 officially recognized world records in athletics. No other arena in the world comes close to that number and hopefully, you can have your own record finishing the adidas Stockholm Marathon at this stadium.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 12. CREATE A VARIABLE USING REGEX}

\CommentTok{\# Using a regular expression to classify events as single{-}day or multi{-}day.}
\CommentTok{\# If the date string contains a dash (like "14 May {-} 16 May"), it spans multiple}
\CommentTok{\# days. If there is no dash, it is just one day.}
\CommentTok{\# This is an application of the regex concepts from Lab 5.}

\NormalTok{events\_df\_clean}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{event\_duration\_type }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{ifelse}\NormalTok{(}
  \FunctionTok{grepl}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"{-}"}\NormalTok{, events\_df\_clean}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{date),}
  \StringTok{"Multi{-}day event"}\NormalTok{,}
  \StringTok{"Single{-}day event"}
\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Checking the result.}

\NormalTok{events\_df\_clean[, }\FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"event\_name"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"date"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"event\_duration\_type"}\NormalTok{)]}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 13. DOWNLOAD ONE EVENT IMAGE (non{-}text file)}

\CommentTok{\# To include an example of downloading a non{-}text file, I download the main}
\CommentTok{\# image from the first event page. The image URL is stored in the og:image}
\CommentTok{\# meta tag, which is a common way websites define their preview image.}

\NormalTok{test\_event\_url }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ events\_df\_clean}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{link[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}

\NormalTok{test\_event\_response }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{GET}\NormalTok{(test\_event\_url)}

\NormalTok{test\_event\_html }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{content}\NormalTok{(test\_event\_response, }\AttributeTok{as =} \StringTok{"text"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{encoding =} \StringTok{"UTF{-}8"}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{test\_event\_dom }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{htmlParse}\NormalTok{(test\_event\_html)}

\NormalTok{test\_image\_url }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{xpathSApply}\NormalTok{(}
\NormalTok{  test\_event\_dom,}
  \StringTok{"//meta[@property=\textquotesingle{}og:image\textquotesingle{}]"}\NormalTok{,}
\NormalTok{  xmlGetAttr,}
  \StringTok{"content"}
\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{test\_image\_url}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\NormalTok{  image\_response }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{GET}\NormalTok{(}
\NormalTok{    test\_image\_url[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{],}
    \FunctionTok{write\_disk}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"visitstockholm\_event\_image.jpg"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{overwrite =} \ConstantTok{TRUE}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{  )}
  
\NormalTok{  image\_response}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{status\_code}
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}

\CommentTok{\# 16. VISUALIZATION}

\FunctionTok{png}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"visitstockholm\_category\_plot.png"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{width =} \DecValTok{1400}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{height =} \DecValTok{900}\NormalTok{)}

\FunctionTok{par}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{mar =} \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{18}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{))}

\FunctionTok{barplot}\NormalTok{(}
\NormalTok{  category\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{number\_of\_events,}
  \AttributeTok{names.arg =}\NormalTok{ category\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{category,}
  \AttributeTok{horiz =} \ConstantTok{TRUE}\NormalTok{,}
  \AttributeTok{las =} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{,}
  \AttributeTok{main =} \StringTok{"Number of Visit Stockholm events by category"}\NormalTok{,}
  \AttributeTok{xlab =} \StringTok{"Number of events"}\NormalTok{,}
  \AttributeTok{cex.names =} \FloatTok{0.9}
\NormalTok{)}

\FunctionTok{dev.off}\NormalTok{()}

\CommentTok{\# 17. GEOCODING WITH THE NOMINATIM API}

\CommentTok{\# I enriched the dataset with latitude and longitude using the Nominatim API}
\CommentTok{\# from OpenStreetMap. This is free to use but requires a User{-}Agent header.}
\CommentTok{\#}
\CommentTok{\# For each event, I build a geocoding query:}
\CommentTok{\# {-} If I have a street address, I use street address + postal code + city + Sweden.}
\CommentTok{\# {-} If not, I fall back to using the location name + Stockholm + Sweden.}

\NormalTok{events\_df\_clean}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{geocode\_query }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{ifelse}\NormalTok{(}
  \FunctionTok{is.na}\NormalTok{(events\_df\_clean}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{street\_address),}
  \FunctionTok{paste}\NormalTok{(events\_df\_clean}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{location, }\StringTok{"Stockholm, Sweden"}\NormalTok{),}
  \FunctionTok{paste}\NormalTok{(events\_df\_clean}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{street\_address, events\_df\_clean}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{postal\_code, events\_df\_clean}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{city, }\StringTok{"Sweden"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Checking the queries before sending them.}

\NormalTok{events\_df\_clean[, }\FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"event\_name"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"location"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"street\_address"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"postal\_code"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"city"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"geocode\_query"}\NormalTok{)]}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# To avoid making the same API request twice for the same address,}
\CommentTok{\# I geocode only the unique queries and then merge the results back in.}

\NormalTok{unique\_queries }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{unique}\NormalTok{(events\_df\_clean}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{geocode\_query)}

\NormalTok{geo\_df }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{data.frame}\NormalTok{(}
  \AttributeTok{geocode\_query =}\NormalTok{ unique\_queries,}
  \AttributeTok{lat =} \ConstantTok{NA}\NormalTok{,}
  \AttributeTok{lon =} \ConstantTok{NA}\NormalTok{,}
  \AttributeTok{stringsAsFactors =} \ConstantTok{FALSE}
\NormalTok{)}

\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ (i }\ControlFlowTok{in} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{:}\FunctionTok{nrow}\NormalTok{(geo\_df)) \{}
  
  \CommentTok{\# URLencode makes sure spaces and special characters are safe for a URL.}
  
\NormalTok{  query }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{URLencode}\NormalTok{(geo\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{geocode\_query[i])}
  
\NormalTok{  api\_url }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{paste0}\NormalTok{(}
    \StringTok{"https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?q="}\NormalTok{,}
\NormalTok{    query,}
    \StringTok{"\&format=json\&limit=1"}
\NormalTok{  )}
  
  \FunctionTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{paste}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Geocoding address"}\NormalTok{, i, }\StringTok{"of"}\NormalTok{, }\FunctionTok{nrow}\NormalTok{(geo\_df)))}
  
  \CommentTok{\# Nominatim requires a User{-}Agent header to identify the application.}
  \CommentTok{\# Without this, the API will reject the request.}
  
\NormalTok{  api\_response }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{GET}\NormalTok{(}
\NormalTok{    api\_url,}
    \FunctionTok{add\_headers}\NormalTok{(}
      \StringTok{"User{-}Agent"} \OtherTok{=} \StringTok{"visit{-}stockholm{-}student{-}project/1.0"}
\NormalTok{    )}
\NormalTok{  )}
  
\NormalTok{  api\_text }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{content}\NormalTok{(api\_response, }\AttributeTok{as =} \StringTok{"text"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{encoding =} \StringTok{"UTF{-}8"}\NormalTok{)}
  
\NormalTok{  api\_json }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{fromJSON}\NormalTok{(api\_text)}
  
  \CommentTok{\# If the API returned a result, I store the latitude and longitude.}
  
  \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ (}\FunctionTok{length}\NormalTok{(api\_json) }\SpecialCharTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{0} \SpecialCharTok{\&\&} \FunctionTok{nrow}\NormalTok{(api\_json) }\SpecialCharTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{) \{}
\NormalTok{    geo\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{lat[i] }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ api\_json}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{lat[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{    geo\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{lon[i] }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ api\_json}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{lon[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{  \}}
  
  \CommentTok{\# Pausing between requests — Nominatim has a usage policy that asks}
  \CommentTok{\# for no more than one request per second.}
  
  \FunctionTok{Sys.sleep}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Merging the geolocation results back into the event dataset.}

\NormalTok{events\_df\_final }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{merge}\NormalTok{(}
\NormalTok{  events\_df\_clean,}
\NormalTok{  geo\_df,}
  \AttributeTok{by =} \StringTok{"geocode\_query"}\NormalTok{,}
  \AttributeTok{all.x =} \ConstantTok{TRUE}
\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# The geocode\_query column was only needed as a helper for the merge,}
\CommentTok{\# so I remove it from the final dataset.}

\NormalTok{events\_df\_final}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{geocode\_query }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \ConstantTok{NULL}

\CommentTok{\# Checking the final dataset.}

\FunctionTok{head}\NormalTok{(events\_df\_final)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

##                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              event_description
## 1                                                                                                                                                        Linkin Park, who recently received the "Favorite Rock Song" award at the American Music Awards, can now confirm that their acclaimed From Zero World Tour will be extended with new selected European dates in 2026. The tour will kick off on Friday, May 29, with a highly anticipated concert at 3Arena in Stockholm – the band's only performance in the Nordic region next year.
## 2                                                                                                                                                                    In recent years, Dermot Kennedy has gone from being a busker on the street corners of Dublin to becoming one of the most beloved voices in the world. The journey is well-known but still remarkable. When you hear his raspy, almost weathered voice carry melodies filled with both fire and vulnerability, it’s easy to understand how everything happened so quickly.
## 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The Art of Loving
## 4                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Photo: Robert Höglund
## 5                                                                                                                                                                                                      The artist Kim Andreas Roland Berger has been awarded the Fredrik Roos Art Grant for 2026. In connection with the award, Artipelag presents Roland Berger’s grant exhibition, Accumulated Stacks. Kim Andreas Roland Berger (b. 1993 in Oslo) uses drawing, painting and sculpture in his material-based and process-oriented practice.
## 6 At the turn of the 20th century, Alphonse Mucha was one of the most famous artists in Europe. A key figure of Art Nouveau and the inventor of an original style of graphic art, his work combined female beauty and stylised nature with a resolutely innovative composition and typography. The “Mucha style” has been a source of fascination ever since it was created and was applied to a variety of artworks and objects that adorned art lovers’ homes around the world at the time. Welcome to an immersive experience for all ages!

\CommentTok{\# 18. SAVE THE FINAL DATASET}

\CommentTok{\# Saving the final dataset as a CSV file.}
\CommentTok{\# I use write\_excel\_csv instead of write\_csv because it adds a BOM (byte order mark)}
\CommentTok{\# at the start of the file. This helps Excel open the file correctly and display}
\CommentTok{\# Swedish characters like å, ä, ö without them turning into strange symbols.}
\CommentTok{\# I had this problem with a regular write\_csv and this fixed it.}

\FunctionTok{write\_excel\_csv}\NormalTok{(}
\NormalTok{  events\_df\_final,}
  \StringTok{"visitstockholm\_events\_final.csv"}
\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
